x: God Almighty says: The Inevitable Hour in which matters will be decided and rewards for deeds will be required.

What is the Inevitable? He says: What is the Inevitable Hour? It was mentioned that the Arabs say: When he knew the Inevitable when and the Inevitable when, and with the kasra they have the same meaning in the three languages. They also say: The thing has become due to him if it is obligatory, so he has rights. The first Inevitable is raised by the second, because the second is like a metaphor for it, as if he was amazed by it, so he said: The Inevitable, what is it! Just as it is said: Zaid, what is Zaid! The second Inevitable is raised by what, and what means which, and what is raised by the second Inevitable, and similar to it in the Qur’an: And the companions of the right hand, what are the companions of the right hand? (al-Waqi’ah 56:27), and The Calamity * What is the Calamity? [1-2], so what is in the position of raising by the second Inevitable and the first by the whole speech after it.
And in a similar manner to what we said about His statement, The Inevitable, the people of interpretation said.
Who said that?

c: Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement: The Inevitable, he said: It is one of the names of the Day of Resurrection. God has made it great and warned His servants about it.

c: Abu Kuraib told us: Ibn Yaman told us, on the authority of Sharik, on the authority of Jabir, on the authority of Ikrimah, who said:
m: The Inevitable means the Resurrection.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his saying, The Inevitable means the Hour will make every worker’s deeds due.

c: Ibn Abd al-A’la told me: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada:
m: Al-Haqqah means: The deeds of every people have been made due.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid narrated to us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement, The Inevitable, meaning the Resurrection.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told me, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, The Inevitable - what is the Inevitable? And the Calamity - what is the Calamity? And the Event, and the Tragedy and the Deafening Deafening. He said: All of this is on the Day of Resurrection, the Hour. And God recited, “Its coming will not be denied. Abasing and raising.” (al-Waqi’ah 56:2-3), and the abasing among these also lowered the people of the Fire, and we do not know of anyone lowered than the people of the Fire, nor more humiliated or disgraced. And it raised the people of Paradise, and we do not know of anyone more noble or more honorable than the people of Paradise.

x: And His saying:
h
And what will make you know what the Inevitable
is? God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: What will make you know what the Inevitable is?

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, who said:
m: What is in the Qur’an and what makes you know, he did not inform him of it, and what was and what makes you know, he informed him of it.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement,
h
And what will make you know what the Inevitable
is? is a glorification of the Day of Resurrection, as you hear.

x: And His statement:
h
Thamud and Aad denied the terrible calamity

. God Almighty says: Thamud, the people of Salih, and Aad, the people of Hud, denied the hour in which the hearts of the servants would be struck by its attack upon them. Al-Qari'ah is also one of the names of the Day of Resurrection. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement, Thamud and Aad denied the calamity, meaning the Hour.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement,
h
Thamud and Aad denied the terrible calamity
. He said: The terrible calamity is the Day of Resurrection.

x: God Almighty says,
h
As for Thamud
, the people of Salih, God destroyed them with tyranny.
The people of interpretation differed about the meaning of the tyranny with which God destroyed the Thamud.
Some of them said: It is their tyranny and disbelief in God.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding the statement of God Almighty, So they were destroyed by the tyrant, he said: by sins.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement,
h
As for Thamud
, they were destroyed by their transgression, then he recited the statement of God, Thamud denied it because of their transgression
r
(Ash-Shams: 11)

, and he said: This transgression is their transgression and their disbelief in the signs of God, the transgression is their transgression in which they transgressed in disobeying God and opposing the Book of God.

x: Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is: They were destroyed by the shout that exceeded the limits of shouting and overwhelmed it.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement,
h
As for Thamud
, they were destroyed by the transgressor, God sent a blast upon them that destroyed them.

c: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada,
m: By the tyrant, he said: God sent a single blast upon them that destroyed them. The first of the two opinions on this matter is the correct opinion of the one who said: The meaning of this is: So they were destroyed by the overwhelming blast. We say this is more correct, because God only spoke about Thamud in the sense that He destroyed them, just as He spoke about ‘Ad in the sense that He destroyed them. He said: And as for ‘Ad, they were destroyed by a furious, violent wind. If the speech about Thamud had been about the reason for which He destroyed them, then the speech about ‘Ad would also have been likewise, since it was in one context. And in His following that with His speech about ‘Ad that their destruction was by the wind, there is clear evidence that His speech about Thamud is what I have explained.

x: And His statement:
h
And as for ‘Ad

, they were destroyed by a furious, violent wind. God Almighty says: As for ‘Ad, the people of Hud, God destroyed them by a furious, violent wind, which is a very strong and violent wind with intense cold. Violent means: it was violent towards its treasurers in the blowing, so it exceeded in intensity and violentness its known amount of blowing and cold. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his statement, And as for ‘Aad, they were destroyed by a furious, violent wind, meaning: by a cold, destructive wind that raged against them without mercy or blessing, constant and never easing.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
And as for ‘Ad
, they were destroyed by a violent, furious wind. The violent, cold wind lashed at them until it pierced their hearts.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Musa ibn al-Musayyab, on the authority of Shahr ibn Hawshab, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said:
m: God never sent a wind except by a measure, nor did He ever send down a drop except by a mithqal, except on the day of Noah and the day of Aad. The water on the day of Noah overflowed its reservoirs, and they had no way to reach it. Then he recited: Indeed, when the water overflowed, We carried you in the floating ship (al-Haqqah 69:11), and the wind overpowered its reservoirs, and they had no way to reach it. Then he recited: by a furious, violent wind.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us: Abu Sinan told us, on the authority of more than one person, on the authority of Ali ibn Abi Talib,
m: may God be pleased with him, who said: Not a drop of water came down except by measure at the hands of an angel. Then, on the day of Noah, permission was given to the water without the reservoirs, so the water overflowed the mountains and came out. That is what God said: When the water overflowed, We carried you in the floating ship. And nothing came down from the wind except by measure at the hands of an angel except on the day of Aad, for he gave them permission without the reservoirs, so it came out. That is what God said: A furious, violent wind that overcame the reservoirs.

c: Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, with a violent, furious wind, he said: The violent wind means the severe wind, and the violent wind means the oppressive wind that overcame them and subdued them.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, severe, he said: intense.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid narrated to us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement, with a violent wind, meaning: a cold, violent wind that struck them without mercy or blessing.

x: And His statement,
h
He subjected them to them for seven nights and eight days in succession
, God Almighty says, He subjected those winds to the ‘Ad people for seven nights and eight days in succession.
Some of them said: He meant by that in succession.
Who said that?

c: Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his statement, and eight days in succession, meaning: in succession.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, his statement, decisive, he said: successive.

c: Ibn Hamid told us:
m: Hakam, on the authority of Amr, on the authority of Mansour, on the authority of Abu Muammar, on the authority of Ibn Masoud:
h
And eight consecutive days
. He said: Consecutive.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Jarir told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Abu Muammar, on the authority of Abdullah bin Masoud,
m: similar to the hadith of Muhammad bin Amr.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Abd al-Rahman told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Abu Muammar, on the authority of Abdullah, Hasuma he said:
m: successively. He said: Yahya bin Saeed Al-Qattan told us, he said:

c: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Samak bin Harb, on the authority of Ikrimah,
m: regarding his statement: decisive, he said: successively.

c: Ibn Al-Muthanna told us: Muhammad Ibn Jaʿfar told us: Shuʿbah told us, on the authority of Samak Ibn Harb, on the authority of ʿIkrimah, that he said
m: regarding this verse,
h
And eight consecutive days
, he said: consecutive.

c: Nasr bin Ali told us, he said: My father told us, he said: Khalid bin Qais told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: h
And eight consecutive days
, he said: consecutive, with no break.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement,
h
And eight consecutive days
, he said: consecutive, with no slackening in them.

c: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding His statement, decisive, he said: permanent.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Mansour, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Abu Muammar Abdullah bin Sakhbara, on the authority of Ibn Masoud:
m: Days of judgment. He said: Consecutive.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, he said: Mujahid said:
m: Days decisive he said: successively.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan,
m: Days of judgment, he said: successive, in days of misfortune
r
(Fussilat 41:16)
, he said: unlucky.

x: Others said: What he meant by his saying, decisive is the wind, and that it cuts off everything that harms anyone, and he made this decisiveness an attribute of the wind.
Who said that?

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said
m: about His statement,
h
And eight decisive days

, he said: It decided them and did not leave a single one of them. He said: That decisive is like the one who says: Decide this matter. He said: And there were eight of them who had a characteristic that would take them in every direction. He said: Musa bin Uqbah said: So when the punishment came to them, they said: Arise, let us repel this punishment from our people. He said: So they stood up and lined up in the valley, and God inspired the angel of the wind to uproot one of them every day, and he recited the statement of God, He subjected it to them for seven nights and eight days in succession, until he reached empty palm trees. He said: So the wind would pass by the caravan and turn it and its load around, then it would carry them away in the sky, then it would throw them down on their heads. He recited the statement of God, So when they saw it as a cloud approaching their valleys, they said, ‘This is a cloud bringing us rain’ (al-Ahqaf 46:24). He said: And the rain had been withheld from them, so he recited until he reached, Palmyra will destroy all of it. “A thing by the command of her Lord” (al-Ahqaf 46:25). He said: And the wind did not take off from those eight every day except one. He said: So when God punished the people of Aad, God left one to warn the people. He said: A woman had seen her people, and they said to her: You too? She said: I moved away on the mountain. He said: And it was said to her afterward: You have submitted and you have seen, so how can you not see the punishment of God? She said: I do not know anything except that I submit one night, Surat al-Haqqah 69:7 He subjected it to them for seven nights and eight days in succession, so you would see the people therein fallen down as if they were hollow trunks of palm trees. a night with no wind. The more correct of the two opinions on this, in my opinion, is the opinion of the one who said: What he meant by his saying hasoum is successive, due to the consensus of the jurists among the people of interpretation on that.

x: Some of the people of Arabic used to say: hasoom means succession, if something is successive and its beginning is not cut off from its end, it is called hasoum. He said: And it was taken, and God knows best, from hasamah al-da’a: if its owner is cauterized, because it is flesh that is cauterized with an iron, then it is continued on it. And his saying,
h
Then you will see the people therein fallen down

, means: So you will see, O Muhammad, the people of Ad in those seven decisive nights and eight days fallen down, having perished. As if they were hollow trunks of palm trees, meaning: As if they were the roots of palm trees that had been destroyed.

c: As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: As if they were hollow trunks of palm trees, meaning the roots of palm trees.

x: And His statement:
h
Do you see any remnant of them
? God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: Do you see, O Muhammad, any remnant of the people of Hud? It was said: What was meant by that was:
h
Do you see any remnant of them
Some of the people of Basra who were knowledgeable in the speech of the Arabs said: The meaning of that is:
h
Do you see any remnant of them
? And he said: Its metaphor is the metaphor of the tyrant, a source.
God Almighty says, And Pharaoh came to Egypt. The reciters differed in their recitation of His statement,
h
And before him
. The majority of the reciters of Medina, Kufa, and Mecca, except for Al-Kisa’i, read it as
h
And before him

with a fat-ha on the qaf and a sukoon on the ba’, meaning: And there came before Pharaoh from the nations who denied the signs of God, such as the people of Noah, Aad, Thamud, and the people of Lot with their sin. The majority of the reciters of Basra and Al-Kisa’i read it as
h
And before him

with a kasra on the qaf and a fat-ha on the ba’, meaning: And there came with Pharaoh from the people of his country, Egypt, from the Copts. The correct thing to say about this, in my opinion, is that they are two well-known readings with correct meanings, so whichever one the reader recites, he is correct. His saying, And the villages that were destroyed by sin, means: And the villages that were destroyed by their work, so that their top became their bottom.

By sin, meaning by sin, and their sin was: their coming to men from behind. And in a similar manner to what we said about the meaning of His statement, and the overturned ones, the people of interpretation said.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement,
h
And Pharaoh and those before him and the overturned cities came refers to the village of Lot
. In some readings, And Pharaoh and those with him came.

c: Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said
m: about His statement,
h
And Pharaoh and those before him and the overturned cities brought the sinful thing

, he said: The overturned cities are the people of Lot, their city and their crops. And about His statement, And the overturned cities He caused to fall (al-Najm 53:53), he said: He caused them to fall from the sky: He threw them from the sky. God inspired Gabriel, peace be upon him, so he uprooted them from the earth, along with their city, then he threw them to the sky, then he turned them to the ground, then he followed them with rocks, stones, as God said, Stones of hard clay, layered, marked
r
. He said: The marked ones are those prepared for punishment.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his statement,
h
And Pharaoh and those before him and the overturned cities brought the wrongdoing
, meaning the deniers.

c: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada:
m: And the overturned ones are the people of Lut, whose land was overturned. And what we said about his saying with the wrong one was said by the people of interpretation.

x: Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us
m: both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, with the sin he said: the mistakes.

evidence.text: The reciters differed in their recitation of His statement, And before him.

The majority of the reciters of Medina, Kufa, and Mecca, except for Al-Kisa’i, read it as And before him with a fat-ha on the qaf and a sukoon on the ba’, meaning: And there came before Pharaoh from the nations who denied the signs of God, such as the people of Noah, Aad, Thamud, and the people of Lot with their sin.

The majority of the reciters of Basra and Al-Kisa’i read it as And before him with a kasra on the qaf and a fat-ha on the ba’, meaning: And there came with Pharaoh from the people of his country, Egypt, from the Copts.

x: And His saying:
h
So they disobeyed the Messenger of their Lord
, God Almighty says: So these people whom God mentioned, namely Pharaoh and those before him and the overturned cities, disobeyed the Messenger of their Lord. His statement,
h
So He seized them with a severe seizure

, means: So their Lord seized them because of their denial of His messengers with a severe seizure, meaning an increasing, severe seizure, from their saying, Arbait, if he increased what he gave in interest. It is said, Arbait, so interest has increased you. Silver and gold have increased. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us
m: both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, A severe seizure. He said: Severe.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his statement,
h
So He seized them with a severe seizure
, meaning a severe seizure.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said
m: about the statement of God, So He seized them with a mighty grip, he said: Just as there is a hill in goodness, so there is a hill in evil. He said: He raised them up: He increased them up. And he recited the statement of God, the Almighty, the Majestic: Those who disbelieved and averted from the way of God - We will increase for them punishment over the punishment (al-Nahl 16:88). And he recited the statement of God, the Almighty, the Majestic: And those who were guided - He increased them in guidance and gave them their righteousness
r
(Muhammad 47:17)
. He said: A hill for these people is good and for those people is evil.

x: And His saying:
h
When the water overflowed

, We carried you in the moving ship. God Almighty says: When the water increased and exceeded its known limit, it was for him, and that was during the time of the flood. It was said that it actually increased above everything by fifteen cubits. Mention who said that, and who said about his saying he transgressed like what we said.

c: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
When the water overflowed
, he said: We were informed that it overflowed fifteen cubits above everything.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement,
h
When the water overflowed
, We carried you in the moving ship. That was during the time of Noah, the water overflowed everything, fifteen cubits, the extent of everything.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Yaqub al-Qummi told us, on the authority of Jaʿfar ibn Abi al-Mughira, on the authority of Saʿid ibn Jubayr,
m: that
h
when the water overflowed
, it became angry with God’s anger, so it overflowed the reservoirs, and something came out that they did not know what it was.

c: Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his statement,
h
When the water overflowed
, We carried you in the moving ship, he only says: when it increased.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his statement,
h
When the water overflowed
, meaning the water increased on the nights when God drowned the people of Noah.

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us
m: both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement,
h
When the water overflowed
, We carried you. Muhammad ibn Amr said in his hadith: it overflowed, and Al-Harith said: it appeared.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn bin Al-Faraj,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd narrated to us, on the authority of Al-Dahhak, regarding his statement,
h
when the water overflowed
, meaning it increased and rose. His saying,
h
We carried you in the ship
, means:
h
We carried you in the ship
that sails in the water. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.

x: Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement,
h
We carried you in the ship
. The ship is the ship.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement,
h
We carried you in the ship

, and the ship is the ship of Noah in which you were carried. It was also said: We carried you, so He addressed those about whom the Qur’an was revealed, and their ancestors carried Noah and his children, because those who were addressed with that were the children of those who were carried in the ship, so the carrying of those who were carried in it from the ancestors was for their offspring, as we have explained of similar examples in many places in this book of ours.

x: And His statement,
h
That We may make it a reminder for you

, means: That We may make the sailing ship in which We carried you a reminder for you, meaning a lesson and an admonition from which you may learn. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement, So
h
that We may make it a reminder for you
, so God kept it as a reminder, a lesson, and a sign until the first of this nation looked at it. How many ships there were after the ship of Noah that turned to ashes. His saying,
h
And a hearing ear receives it
, means a memory that understands what it hears from God. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.

x: Who said that?

c: Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: h
And a hearing ear will receive it
, meaning: a memorizer.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: h
And a hearing ear will receive it
, meaning: hearing, and that is the announcement.

x: Who said that?

c: Nasr bin Ali told us, he said: My father told us, he said: Khalid bin Qais told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
And a hearing ear receives it
. He said: An ear that understands from God.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement,
h
and a hearing ear receives it
, an ear that understands from God, so it benefits from what it hears from the Book of God.

c: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada:
m: A listening ear means: an ear that heard and understood what it heard.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid narrated to us, who said: Al-Dahhak says regarding His statement,
h
And a hearing ear will receive it
, “An ear heard it and it will receive it.”

c: Ali bin Sahl told us: Al-Walid bin Muslim told us, on the authority of Ali bin Hawshab, who said:
m: I heard Makhul say: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited: ‘And a listening ear will retain it.’ Then he turned to Ali and said: ‘I asked God to make it your ear.’ Ali, may God be pleased with him, said: ‘So I did not hear anything from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that I forgot.’”

c: Muhammad bin Khalaf told me, he said: Bishr bin Adam told me, he said: Abdullah bin Al-Zubayr told us, he said: Abdullah bin Rustum told me, he said:
m: “I heard Buraydah say: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say to Ali: O Ali, God has commanded me to bring you close and not to keep you away, and to teach you and for you to understand, and it is God’s right that you understand. He said: Then the verse ‘and a listening ear will receive it’ was revealed.”

c: Muhammad bin Khalaf told me, he said: Al-Hasan bin Hammad told us, he said: Ismail bin Ibrahim Abu Yahya Al-Taimi told us, on the authority of Fadil bin Abdullah, on the authority of Abu Dawud, on the authority of Buraidah Al-Aslami, he said:
m: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say to Ali: God has commanded me to teach you and to bring you close and not to be harsh with you or to keep you away, then he mentioned something similar.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement,
h
And a hearing ear receives it

, he said: A hearing ear who is wary of God’s sins lest God punish them for them, as He punished those who came before them. It hears it and it receives it. Rather, the hearts receive what the ears hear of good and evil by way of awareness.

x: God Almighty says: Then when the Trumpet is blown Israfil with a single blast which is the first blast.
And the earth and the mountains were lifted up and crushed with a single crushing. He says: They were shaken with a single earthquake.
Ibn Zayd used to say about this:

c: Yunus told me that Ibn Wahb told us that
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement,
h
And the earth and the mountains were borne away and were crushed with a single crushing

, he said: They became dust. It was also said: They were crushed, and he mentioned before the mountains and the earth, and they are a group, and he did not say: They were crushed, because he made the mountains like a single thing, as the poet said: They are two masters who claim to be our masters, but they will only rule us if their sheep are wealthy. And as it was said: The heavens and the earth were joined together (al-Anbiya 21:30).

x: On that Day the Event will occur. God Almighty says: On that Day the Hour will be shouted, and the Resurrection will take place.
God Almighty says: And the heaven will split open, and on that Day it will be fragile. He says: Split and cracked. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Musa bin Abdul Rahman Al-Masruqi told me: Abu Usamah told us, on the authority of Al-Ajlah, who said:
m: I heard Ad-Dahhak bin Muzahim say: When the Day of Resurrection comes, God will command the lowest heaven with its inhabitants, and the angels in it will descend, and they will surround the earth and whoever is on it, then the second, then the third, then the fourth, then the fifth, then the sixth, then the seventh, and they will be arranged in rows below each other. Then the highest angel will descend on its left side, Hell. When the people of the earth see it, they will call out, and they will not come to any region of the earth except that they will find seven rows of angels, so they will return to the place where they were. This is the saying of God: “Indeed, I fear for you the Day of Calling * The Day you will turn back, fleeing. You will have no protector from God”
r

, and this is His saying: And your Lord will come with the angels, rank upon rank, and that Day Hell will be brought forth (al-Fajr 89:22-23), and His saying: “O company of jinn and mankind, if you are able to pass beyond the regions of the heavens and the earth, then pass. You will not be able to do so except by authority.” (al-Rahman 55:33), and this is His saying:
h
And the heaven will be split open
, and that Day it will be fragile, and the angels will be over its corners.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his statement,
h
And the heaven will be split open
, and on that Day it will be fragile, meaning: torn apart and weak.

x: And the King is over its corners. God Almighty says: And the King is over the edges of the sky when it splits and its borders. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his statement,
h
And the angels are on its edges
, meaning: And the angels are on the edges of the sky when it splits, and it is said on the edge of everything that splits from it.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement,
h
And the angels are over its corners
, he said: its edges.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Yaqub told us, on the authority of Jaʿfar, on the authority of Saʿid,
m: regarding his statement,
h
And the angels are over its corners
, he said: on the edges of the sky.

c: Musa bin Abdul Rahman Al-Masruqi told me: Abu Usamah told us, on the authority of Al-Ajlah, who said:
m: I said to Al-Dahhak: What are its edges? He said: Its edges.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
And the angels are on its edges
on its borders.

c: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar:
m: h
And the king is over its corners
. He said: It has reached me that it is its regions. Qatada said: Over its sides.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan:
m: h
And the king is over its corners
. He said: Its regions.

c: Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Ashib told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, on the authority of Ata’ bin Al-Sa’ib, on the authority of Saeed bin Al-Musayyab:
m: The edges of the sky are the corners. He said: Al-Ashib told us, he said:

c: Abu Uwana told us, on the authority of Ata’ bin Al-Sa’ib, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair,
m: h
And the king is over its corners
, he said: over what he has not eaten of it.

c: Muhammad bin Sinan Al-Qazzaz told us, he said: Husayn Al-Ashqar told us, he said: Abu Kudayna told us, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Sa’id bin Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement,
h
And the king is over its corners
, he said: Over what he has not yet eaten of it. And His statement,
h
And eight will bear the Throne of your Lord above them that Day
, the people of interpretation differed as to who was meant by His statement, eight.

x: Some of them said: What was meant by it were eight rows of angels, and no one knows their number except God.
Who said that?

c: Abu Kurayb told us: Talq told us, on the authority of Zuhair, on the authority of Al-Suddi, on the authority of Abu Malik, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: h
And eight will bear the Throne of your Lord above them that Day
. He said: Eight rows of angels, and no one knows their number except God.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding His statement,
h
And eight will bear the Throne of your Lord above them that Day
, he said: They are the rows behind the rows.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Yahya bin Wadh told us: Al-Hussein told us, on the authority of Yazid, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement,
h
And eight will bear the Throne of your Lord above them that Day
, he said: Eight rows of angels.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid narrated to us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement,
h
And eight will bear the Throne of your Lord above them that Day
, some of them said: Eight rows, and no one knows their number except God.

x: Some of them said: Eight angels with the creation of the mountain goat.
Others said: Rather, he meant eight angels.
Who said that?

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding His statement,
h
And eight will bear the Throne of your Lord above them that Day

, he said: Eight angels. He said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Four will bear it today, and on the Day of Resurrection, eight will bear it. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Their feet will be on the seventh earth, and their shoulders will come out of the heavens, over which is the Throne.” Ibn Zayd said: The four said: It has reached us that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: When God created them, He said: Do you know why I created you? They said: Our Lord created us for what You will. He said to them: You will bear My Throne. Then He said: Ask Me for whatever power you wish, and I will place it in you. One of them said: The Throne of our Lord was over the water, so place it in the power of the water. He said: I have placed in you the power of the water.

x: Another said: Place it in the power of the heavens. He said: I have placed in you the power of the heavens.
Another said: Place it in the power of the earth. He said: I have placed in you the power of the earth and the mountains.

Another said: Place it in the power of the winds. He said: I have placed in you the power of The winds, then he said: Carry! So they placed the throne on their shoulders, and it did not move. K said: Then another flag came, and it was their flag that they asked for strength, so he said to them: Say: There is no power or strength except with God, so they said: There is no power or strength except with God, so God put in them a power and strength that their knowledge did not reach, so they carried.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, who said:
m: It has reached us that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Today they are four, meaning the bearers of the Throne, and when the Day of Resurrection comes, God will support them with four more, so they will be eight. And God said:
h
And eight will bear the Throne of your Lord above them that Day

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Jarir told us, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Maysarah,
m: regarding his statement,
h
And eight will bear the Throne of your Lord above them that Day
, he said: Their feet will be on the borders, unable to raise their eyes from the rays of light.

x: And His statement, On that Day you will be brought before Him, and nothing of yours will be hidden. God Almighty says: On that Day, O people, you will be brought before your Lord. It was said: Three presentations.
Who said that?

c: Al-Hasan bin Qaz’ah Al-Bahili told us: Waki’ bin Al-Jarrah told us: Ali bin Ali Al-Rifai told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan, on the authority of Abu Musa Al-Ash’ari, who said:
m: People will be exposed to three situations. As for the second of them, they will be arguments and excuses. As for the third, at that time the pages will fly into the hands, and I will take hold of his right hand and I will take hold of his left.

c: Mujahid bin Musa told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Sulayman bin Hayyan told us, on the authority of Marwan al-Asghar, on the authority of Abu Wa’il, on the authority of Abdullah, he said:
m: People will be presented on the Day of Resurrection three times: two presentations of excuses and disputes, and the third presentation will be when the pages will fly in the hands.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement,
h
On that Day you will be exposed

, nothing about you will be hidden. It was mentioned to us that the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to say: “People will be exposed three times on the Day of Resurrection. As for two of the exposures, they will involve disputes, excuses, and arguments. As for the third exposure, the scrolls will fly into the hands.”

c: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada,
m: in a similar manner. And His saying,
h
Nothing about you is hidden
, means that He, the Most High, says:
h
Nothing about you is hidden
from God, because He knows all of you and encompasses all of you.

x: God Almighty says: As for he who is given his book of deeds in his right hand, God Almighty says, Read his book.

c: As Yunus bin Abdul A’la told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding God’s statement, Here, read my book, he said: Come.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, he said:
m: Some of the people of knowledge used to say: I found the most intelligent of people to be the one who said: Here, read my book.

x: And his saying, Indeed, I thought that I would meet my account, means: I knew that I would meet my account when I appear before my Lord on the Day of Resurrection. And in a manner similar to what we said in the interpretation of his saying, I thought, the people of interpretation said.
Who said that?

c: Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his statement, Indeed, I thought that I would meet my account, meaning: I was certain.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: Indeed, I thought that I would meet my account. He thought with certainty, so God benefited him with his thought.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, Indeed, I thought that I would meet my account, he said: Indeed, the thought of the believer is certain, and the hope from God is obligatory. Perhaps those will be among the rightly guided (al-Tawbah 9:18), Perhaps he will be among the successful (al-Qasas 28:67).

c: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada:
m: I thought that I would meet my reckoning. He said: Whatever is thought of the Hereafter is knowledge.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Jabir, on the authority of Mujahid, who said:
m: Every thought in the Qur’an, I thought, means I knew.

x: God Almighty says: The one whose affair I have described, and he who was given his book in his right hand, will have a pleasing life, or a life in which there is contentment. So the life was described as pleasing and pleasing, because that is praise for the life, and the Arabs do that in praise and blame, so they say: This is a sleeping night, a concealed secret, and gushing water, so they direct the action to it, and it is originally the object of what is intended of praise or blame. And whoever says that is not permitted to say to the one who strikes struck, or to the one who is struck struck, because there is neither praise nor blame in that.
And his saying: In a high garden means: In a high, lofty garden, and the in in his saying garden is related to the verb to live.
And his saying:
h
Its fruits are within easy reach

means: The fruits that are picked from Paradise are within easy reach and close to the one who picks them. He mentioned that whoever wants its fruit can eat it however he wants, standing or sitting, and nothing will prevent him from it, nor will thorns stand between him and it. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Al-Muthanna told us: Muhammad Ibn Jaʿfar told us: Shuʿbah told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, who said:
m: I heard Al-Bara’ say about this verse, its fruits are within reach. He said: A man may eat its fruits while he is asleep.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement,
h
its fruits are within easy reach
: it is close at hand, so their hands will not be turned away from it, nor will there be thorns.

x: And His statement:
h
Eat and drink at ease for what you sent forth in the days gone by

. Their Lord, may He be glorified, says to them: Eat, O company with whom I am pleased, and whom I admit into My Paradise, from its fruits and the goodness of the foods therein, and drink from its drinks, at ease for you you will not be harmed by what you eat or drink, and you will not need to defecate or urinate from eating that. for what you sent forth in the days gone by. He says: Eat and drink at ease: a reward from God to you, and a recompense for what you sent forth, or for what you sent forth: that is, for what you sent forth in your worldly life for your afterlife of deeds in obedience to God in the days gone by. He says: in the days of the world that have passed and gone. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: God said: Eat and drink at ease for what you put forth in the past days. These days of yours are past days, they are fleeting days that lead to everlasting days, so work in these days, and do good in them if you are able, and there is no power except with God.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement,
h
For what you put forth in the days gone by
, he said: The days of this world, for what they did in them.

x: God Almighty says: And as for he who is given on that Day his book of deeds in his left hand, he will say, Oh, I wish I had not been given my book.
I did not know what my calculations were. He says: I did not know what my calculations were.

And his saying: Oh, would that it had been the final judgment, meaning: I wish that the death I died in this world had been the cessation of everything after it, and that there had been no life or resurrection after it. And judgment is the cessation, and it was said that he wished for the death that would be decreed for him, so that his soul would depart from it. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his saying, Oh, if only it had been the final decision, he wished for death, and there was nothing in this world more hateful to him than death.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, Oh, if only it had been the final judgment, it means death.

x: God Almighty says, informing us about the one who was given his book in his left hand, My wealth did not avail me at all. Meaning that the wealth that he owned in this world did not protect him from God’s punishment at all.

My authority has perished means: My arguments have gone away from me and are lost, so I have no argument to use as evidence. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: My two powers perished from me, meaning: Every proof was lost to me and was of no use to me.

c: Abdul Rahman bin Al-Aswad Al-Tafawi told me, he said: Muhammad bin Rabi’ah told us, on the authority of Al-Nadr bin Arabi, he said:
m: I heard Ikrimah say:
h
My authority has perished from me
. He said: My proof.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement,
h
My two authorities have perished from me
, he said: My proof.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement,
h
My two authorities have perished from me

. By God, not everyone who enters Hell was the leader of a village who collected taxes from it, but God created them, gave them authority over their peers, commanded them to obey God, and forbade them from disobeying God.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid told us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement,
h
My authority has perished from me
, meaning: My proof has gone astray from me.

x: Others said: What is meant by the Sultan in this place is the king.
Who said that?

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding his statement, My two powers have perished from me, he said: The power of the world.

x: And His saying,
h
Take him and chain him
, God Almighty says to His angels from the treasuries of Hell,
h
Take him and chain him
, then roast him in Hell, meaning: Then bring him into the fire of Hell to be roasted in it.
God Almighty says: Then they will burn in Hell.
His saying,
h
Then thread it through a chain seventy cubits long
. He says:
h
Then thread it through a chain seventy cubits long
. God knows best how long it is. It was said that it enters his anus, then exits through his nostrils.
Some of them said: It enters his mouth and exits from his anus.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Bashar told us, he said: Abd al-Rahman told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Naseer bin Dhaluq, he said:
m: I heard Nawf say:
h
In a chain whose length is seventy cubits
. He said: Each cubit is seventy cubits. The cubit is the distance between you and Mecca.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Yahya told us, he said: Sufyan told us, Naseer told us, he said:
m: I heard Nawf say: In the square of Kufa during the emirate of Musʿab ibn al-Zubayr, regarding his statement,
h
In a chain whose length is seventy cubits
, he said: The cubit is seventy spans. The span is the distance between you and Mecca.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Naseer bin Dhaluq Abu Ta’mah, on the authority of Nawf al-Bakali:
m: h
In a chain whose length is seventy cubits
. He said: Each cubit is a fathom, each fathom is further than what is between you and Mecca, and he was at that time in the mosque of Kufa.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement,
h
In a chain whose length is seventy cubits
, so thread it, he said: By the king’s cubit, so thread it. He said: Thread it through his anus until it comes out of his nostrils, so that he cannot stand on his feet.

c: Ibn Al-Muthanna told us: Yaʿmar bin Bashir Al-Manqari told us: Ibn Al-Mubarak told us: Saʿid bin Yazid told us, on the authority of Abu Al-Samh, on the authority of Isa bin Hilal Al-Sadfi, on the authority of Abdullah bin Amr bin Al-ʿAs, who said:
m: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: If a bullet like this - and he pointed to a skull - were sent from the sky to the earth, which is a distance of five hundred years, it would reach the earth before nightfall. And if it were sent from the top of the chain, it would travel for forty autumns, night and day, before reaching its bottom or its base.”

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Ibn al-Mubarak, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of al-Dahhak,
m: So pass it through. He said: The chain is to put the chain in his mouth and exit from his anus. It was also said: Then
h
in a chain whose length is seventy cubits

, so pass it through. The chain is only passed through his mouth, as the Arabs said: I put my head in the skullcap. The skullcap is only put through the head, and as al-A’sha said: If the mirage wore sleeves Rather, the sleeve is covered with a mirage, and the like, and it was said thus so that the listeners would know its meaning, and so that what the speaker meant would not be difficult for the listener.

x: And his saying:
h
He did not believe in God the Almighty
means: Do that to him as a punishment for his disbelief in God in this world, for he did not believe in the oneness of God the Almighty.
God Almighty says, informing us about this wretched man who was given his book in his left hand: In this world, he did not urge people to feed the poor and needy.
And His statement:
h
So he has no close friend here today
, God Almighty says:
h
So he has no close friend here today
, that is, in the Hereafter, meaning, in the Hereafter, meaning, someone close to him who will defend him and help him from the affliction he is in.

c: As Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, in his statement,
h
So he has no close friend here today
, close in the speech of the Arabs.

x: And there is no food except from two washings. God Almighty says: And there is no food for him, just as he was not encouraged in this world to feed the poor, except from two washings, and that is what flows from the pus of the people of Hell.

Some of the Arab scholars from Basra used to say: Every wound that you wash and something comes out of it is called ghaslin. So, al-wasl is derived from al-jarh the wound and al-dabar the anus. The ya and nun were added to it, like afrin. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his statement,
h
And no food except from the pus of the people of Hell

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement,
h
And no food except from two washes
, he said: What comes out of their flesh.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his saying,
h
And no food except from two washings is the worst
, most disgusting, and most abhorrent of food. Ibn Zayd used to say in his statement on that:

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement,
h
And no food except from two streams
, he said: The two streams and the Zaqqum, no one knows what they are.

x: And his saying:
h
None eat it except sinners
, meaning: No one eats food from two washings except sinners, and they are the guilty ones whose sins are disbelief in God.

God Almighty says: The matter is not as you say, you people who deny the Book of God and His Messenger. I swear by all the things that you see and those that you do not see. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding His statement,
h
So I swear by what you see and what you do not see
, he said: I swear by things,
h
so I swear by what you see and what you do not see

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding His statement,
h
So I swear by what you see * and what you do not see
, he said: by what you see and what you do not see.

x: God Almighty says: And what you do not see.

And His statement: Indeed, it is the word of a noble Messenger. God Almighty says: Indeed, this Qur’an is the word of a noble Messenger, and he is Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, reciting it to them.
And His statement:
h
And it is not the statement of a poet

; little do you believe. God Almighty says: This Qur’an is not the statement of a poet because Muhammad is not good at reciting poetry, so you say it is poetry. Little do you believe. He says: You believe in it little, and that is an address from God to the polytheists of Quraysh.

"And it is not the word of a soothsayer. Little do you remember." He says: It is not the word of a soothsayer, because Muhammad is not a soothsayer, so you say: It is from the rhyme of soothsayers. Little do you remember. He says: You learn from it, little do you consider it. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: It is not the word of a poet; little do you believe. God purified him from that and protected him. Nor the word of a soothsayer; little do you remember. God purified him from soothsaying and protected him from it.

x: God Almighty says: But it is a revelation from the Lord of the Worlds that was sent down to him.
Even if you say about us Muhammad" some false sayings, and lie about us.
h
We would have seized him by the right hand

. He says: We would have seized him by force and power from us, then we would have severed the ties of his heart. What he means by that is that He would hasten the punishment and not delay it. It has been said that the meaning of his statement,
h
We would have seized him by the right hand

is: We would have seized him by his right hand. They said: This is a metaphor, and its meaning is: We would have humiliated and degraded him, then after that We would have cut off his aorta. They said: This is like the saying of a person of authority when he wants to belittle someone in front of him to some of his helpers: Take his hand and make him stand up, and do such and such to him. They said: And likewise the meaning of his statement,
h
We would have seized him by the right hand
is: We would have humiliated him as we do to the one whose condition we have described.
And similar to what we said about the meaning of his saying the aorta, the people of interpretation said.
Who said that?

c: Sulayman ibn Abd al-Jabbar told me, he said: Muhammad ibn al-Salt told us, he said: Abu Kudayna told us, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Sa’id ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: h
We would have cut off his aorta
. He said: The arteries of the heart.

c: Ibn Al-Muthanna told us: Muhammad Ibn Jaʿfar told us: Shuʿbah told us, on the authority of ʿAtaʿ, on the authority of Saʿid Ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: with a similar chain of transmission.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Hakam told us, on the authority of Amr, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: similarly.

c: Yaqoub told me, he said: Hisham told us, on the authority of Ata’ bin Al-Sa’ib, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, he said: Ibn Abbas said:
m: The aorta is the strings of the heart.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Abd al-Rahman told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Ata’ ibn al-Sa’ib, on the authority of Sa’id ibn Jubayr,
m: something similar.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said: Mihran told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair,
m: similarly.

c: Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his statement,
h
Then We would have cut off his aorta
, meaning: the vein of the heart.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his statement,
h
Then We would have cut off his aorta
means: a vein in the heart, and it is said: it is a rope in the heart.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, the aorta, he said: the cord of the heart that is in the back.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement,
h
Then We would have cut off his aorta
, he said: the cord of the heart.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid told us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement,
h
We would have cut off his aorta
, the aorta of the heart is a vein in the heart, and if it is cut off, the person dies.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement,
h
Then We would have cut off his aorta

, he said: The aorta is the heart’s tendon to which the heart is attached, and it is what Al-Shamakh Ibn Dirar Al-Taghlabi meant when he said: If you reach me and carry my burden, Araba, then shine with the blood of the jugular vein

x: God Almighty says: There is not one of you, O people, about Muhammad who, if he had fabricated some sayings about Us, We would have seized him by the right hand, then We would have cut his aorta, preventing Us from punishing him, and what We will do to him. And it was said: preventing, so it is plural, and it is an action for one, and one in one word in response to its meaning, because its meaning is the group, and the Arabs make one for one, two, and the group, as it was said: We make no distinction between any of His messengers (al-Baqarah 2:285), and between only occurs with two or more.

And His statement: And indeed, it is a reminder for the righteous. God Almighty says: And indeed, this Qur’an is a reminder, meaning an admonition by which the righteous are reminded and admonished, and they are those who fear God’s punishment by performing His obligations and avoiding His sins. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: And indeed, it is a reminder for the righteous. He said: The Qur’an.

x: And His statement: And indeed, We know that among you are deniers. God Almighty says: And indeed, We know that among you are deniers of this Qur’an, O people.

And His saying: And indeed, it is a regret for the disbelievers. God Almighty says: And indeed, denying it is a regret and remorse for the disbelievers in the Qur’an on the Day of Resurrection. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: And indeed, it is a regret for the disbelievers. That is on the Day of Resurrection.

x: His statement:
h
And it is the certain truth
. He says:
h
And it is the certain truth
in which there is no doubt that it is from God. Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not fabricate it.
His saying:
h
So glorify the name of your Lord
, the Most Great by mentioning your Lord and naming Him, the Most Great, in whose greatness everything is small.

notes.en: Al-Firyābī, Ibn Abī Ḥātim—as cited in Taghlīq al-Taʿlīq (4/347)—and al-Ḥākim (2/501) reported it through ʿAṭāʾ. Al-Suyūṭī attributes it in al-Durr al-Manthūr (p. 429, according to the Maḥmūdī manuscript) to ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Saʿīd ibn Manṣūr.
notes.ar: أخرجه الفريابي، وابن أبي حاتم -كما في تغليق التعليق 4/ 347 - والحاكم 2/ 501 من طريق عطاء به، وعزاه السيوطى فى الدر المنثور -كما في المخطوطة المحمودية ص 429 - إلى عبد بن حميد وابن المنذر وسعيد بن منصور.

notes.en: Al-Suyūṭī attributes it in al-Durr al-Manthūr (6/263) to the author and Ibn al-Mundhir.
notes.ar: عزاه السيوطى فى الدر المنثور 6/ 263 إلى المصنف وابن المنذر.

notes.en: Al-Suyūṭī attributes it in al-Durr al-Manthūr (6/263) to ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd. Al-Ḥākim (2/501) reported it through Warqāʾ, from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid, from Ibn ʿAbbās.
notes.ar: عزاه السيوطى في الدر المنثور 6/ 263 إلى عبد بن حميد، وأخرجه الحاكم 2/ 501 من طريق ورقاء، عن ابن أبي نجيح، عن مجاهد، عن ابن عباس.

notes.en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq reported it in his Tafsīr (2/315) from Maʿmar, from Qatādah. Al-Suyūṭī attributes it in al-Durr al-Manthūr (6/263) to ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd.
notes.ar: أخرجه عبد الرزاق فى تفسيره 2/ 315 عن معمر عن قتادة، وعزاه السيوطى في الدر المنثور 6/ 263 إلى عبد بن حميد.
